title: Helicopter Insurance: Why Rotorcraft Cost About 2% of Hull a Year and How to Qualify for Better Rates
description: Helicopter insurance explained: hull rates around 2% of value, R22 to Bell 206 premiums, the 1,000-hour / 100-in-type benchmark, and training credits of 10–20%.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: Helicopter hull premiums average around **2% of insured hull value** a year for experienced pilots, roughly double the rate for a fixed-gear piston airplane.
Indicative premiums: **Robinson R22 (~$300k hull) $4,000–$8,000**, **Bell 206 (~$1.5M) $15,000–$40,000** a year.
Preferred rates typically need **1,000+ total hours, 100+ in make and model**, and recurrent training every 12 months.
Approved manufacturer training courses can earn **10–20% premium discounts**.

faqs.question: Why is helicopter insurance more expensive than airplane insurance?
faqs.answer: Higher accident frequency, costly dynamic components and fewer insurers. Hull rates average around 2% of value against roughly 1% for piston airplanes. See the [aircraft & aviation insurance explained](/learn/aircraft-aviation-insurance-explained/) hub.

faqs.question: How much is insurance for a Robinson R22?
faqs.answer: Roughly $4,000–$8,000 a year on a ~$300,000 hull, depending on pilot hours, training and use.

faqs.question: How can I lower my helicopter insurance premium?
faqs.answer: Build make-and-model time, complete approved manufacturer training (10–20% credits), fly private rather than commercial missions, and keep a claim-free record.

content.text: Helicopters use the same insurance structure as airplanes: agreed-value hull plus liability, governed by a pilot warranty. The price is very different, though. This spoke of our [aircraft & aviation insurance explained](/learn/aircraft-aviation-insurance-explained/) hub explains why rotorcraft cost more to insure and how owners bring premiums down.

Compare those figures with the 0.9–1.3% hull rate on a typical piston airplane in our [airplane insurance cost](/learn/airplane-insurance-cost/) guide. Higher loss frequency, expensive dynamic components (rotor blades, gearboxes and so on) and a small pool of insurers all push rotorcraft rates up. Commercial, utility and air-medical missions cost substantially more than private flying. Underwriters score each rotorcraft pilot individually, as explained in [what is insurance underwriting](/learn/what-is-insurance-underwriting/), so two R44 owners can get very different quotes.
What Underwriters Want From Helicopter Pilots

items: **Total time:** 1,000+ hours for preferred rates. Low-time pilots pay more and may be offered higher deductibles.
**Make and model time:** 100+ hours in type is a common benchmark.
**Recurrent training:** Certified training every 12 months, with manufacturer courses earning 10–20% credits.
**Use:** Private and business use is cheapest. Instruction, tours, utility and EMS work are rated much higher.

content.title: Training Ownership: Instructors and Clubs
content.text: If you instruct in helicopters you don't own, you need your own non-owned liability policy. See [flight instructor insurance](/qa/flight-instructor-insurance/). Sharing ownership to split a $5,000+ premium? Read [aircraft partnership insurance](/qa/aircraft-partnership-insurance/) first, so that every partner is a named insured.

Check how the policy treats ground-running and hover-taxi damage (in motion or not in motion), external-load or sling operations (usually excluded unless scheduled), and off-airport landings. The general rules on what hull cover does and doesn't pay are in [what does aircraft hull insurance cover](/qa/what-does-aircraft-hull-insurance-cover/). Liability limits should be smooth rather than per-seat where possible (see [smooth vs per-seat liability](/compare/smooth-liability-vs-per-seat-sublimit-aircraft-insurance/)). Helicopter pilots also pay among the highest aviation flat extras on life insurance. See [does life insurance cover private pilots](/qa/does-life-insurance-cover-private-pilots/). Under the FAA's MOSAIC changes, sport pilots can now fly certain helicopters with simplified flight controls. See [light sport aircraft insurance](/learn/light-sport-aircraft-insurance/).
